endpoint.name: Extract web pages
endpoint.summary: Return focused excerpts or full Markdown content from up to 20 public URLs.

fallback.note: One URL; usage settles each further URL.

cost.note: $0.001 per extracted URL; full content costs the same. Live: two readable URLs with full content reported usage sku_extract_excerpts 2; one unreachable URL returned errors[] and an empty usage list. The hold is one URL and usage settles the rest.

objective.note: What you want from the pages; focuses the excerpts. Up to 5,000 characters.

search_queries.note: Keyword queries that focus the excerpts.

max_chars_total.note: Upper bound on excerpt characters across all results.

advanced_settings.note: {full_content: true or {max_chars_per_result}, excerpt_settings {max_chars_per_result}, fetch_policy {max_age_seconds >= 600, timeout_seconds, disable_cache_fallback}}. Full content is off by default.

input.note: A URL that cannot be read returns inside a 200 under errors[] with its error_type and reports no usage. Top-level full_content, excerpts or fetch_policy are rejected; they belong under advanced_settings.

endpoint.capability_description: Extract clean content from web pages

provider.limits: Search, Extract and Entity Search each allow 600 requests per minute on a rolling 60-second window. HTTP 429 is a rate limit; HTTP 402 is insufficient credit, which in-flight requests count against.

siblings.name: Web Scrape
siblings.summary: Scrape any web page and get its content back as clean Markdown (or HTML, or raw HTML) plus title and metadata.

blockAds.note: When true (upstream default), strip ad and cookie-consent elements before capture. Set false to keep them.

excludeTags.note: CSS selectors to drop before capture (for example ["nav", "footer", ".ads"]). Applied after includeTags.

formats.note: Which representations of the page to return. Any combination of: markdown (page content as Markdown), html (the page HTML exactly as the browser received it, including head and script tags). Each requested format is returned under the matching output field. Defaults to both. rawHtml is a deprecated

includeTags.note: CSS selectors to keep. When set, only content matching these selectors is captured (for example ["article", "main"] or ["#content"]).

mobile.note: When true, render the page with a mobile viewport and user agent instead of desktop. Some sites serve materially different content to mobile.

onlyMainContent.note: When true, return only the main article content, stripping navigation, headers, footers, and other boilerplate. Defaults to false to capture the full page.

url.note: The URL of the page to scrape.

waitFor.note: Milliseconds to wait for the page to finish rendering before capture. Use this for JavaScript-heavy pages or single-page apps whose content loads after the initial paint. Capped at 15000 to stay within the request timeout. This wait is time you asked us to spend, so your response takes this much lon

samples.reason: Official Claude Code memory documentation contains auto-memory and MEMORY.md index details; used only as background.
Archive page scraped, but includeTags were ignored and the sidebar rules were not in the output.
Confirmed Cleveragh 8888590 still open with unchanged 24/09/2026 12:00 deadline

siblings.name: Scrape a web page
siblings.summary: Return one page as Markdown, HTML, images or a screenshot.

fallback.note: The curated request allows one basic output and no charged extras.

cost.note: One basic Markdown request consumed one credit live; the current rate card prices the other basic formats at the same base. Settle from reported credits.

formats.note: Choose one basic output; charged JSON, highlights, product and PDF OCR options are excluded.

maxAgeMs.note: Maximum cache age in milliseconds; 0 fetches fresh.

input.note: The curated request permits one basic format. Browser actions and charged extraction options require an own raw tool. A target 404 may still consume the base credit.

siblings.name: Scrape or crawl a web page to clean Markdown for LLMs
siblings.summary: Scrape one URL, a web page or a PDF, into clean, LLM-ready Markdown text and/or HTML. Crawl4AI picks the cheapest engine that works (archive, plain fetch, real browser that renders JavaScript), with optional links, media, metadata and tables; proxies for sites that block datacenters.

cost.note: treg's account price: a flat 0.15 credits per page at every effort (archived, plain, PDF, browser, hard); failures free. The x-c4-cost header settles the charge (0.150 observed live 2026-10-08 at efforts 0, 1, 2 and 3).

not_found.means: the site itself answered 404 or 410: the page does not exist

proxy.note: exit network for sites that block datacenters

country.note: two-letter exit country for isp/residential, e.g. us

parse.note: true for all, or pick {links, media, metadata, tables}

input.note: Most pages answer in 1-2 s; a page that needs a real browser takes 10-30 s, and a failed page ends within about 55 s. A PDF URL returns the PDF's text as Markdown. Images and other binary files answer 422 binary-body within about a second, free. Blocked (403), unreachable (502) and fleet-busy (503) answers are free; retry a 503 after a few seconds.

samples.reason: Live WhatsApp-marketing list exposed low-competition verification jobs (2-5 bids) vs saturated Salla design.
Cheap clean markdown of a trade-data page, including the shipment table.
Returned the full product page as readable markdown in under a second on plain fetch.

siblings.name: Get page contents by URL
siblings.summary: Get the full page contents, summaries, and metadata for a list of URLs.

cost.note: $0.001 per page PER CONTENT TYPE: text, highlights and summary are each billed separately (OBSERVED 2026-08-27: text on one page → costDollars.total 0.001; highlights+summary on one page → 0.002 as {highlights: 0.001, summary: 0.001}). A failed URL is not billed. Platform billing settles the exact costDollars.total.

urls.note: one or more page URLs; each page is billed per content type requested

text.note: true, or {maxCharacters: N} — the page as clean text. $0.001 per page

highlights.note: {query, maxCharacters, numSentences} — the passages most relevant to `query`. $0.001 per page

summary.note: {query} — an AI summary of the page focused on `query`. $0.001 per page

maxAgeHours.note: serve cache if younger than this, else live-crawl; omit for Exa's default freshness

subpages.note: also crawl N linked subpages (each billed as a page)

input.note: each result carries url, title, author, publishedDate and whichever of text / highlights / summary was asked for; `statuses` says per URL whether it came from cache or a live crawl, or failed. Request only the content types you need — each one is a separate $0.001 per page.

samples.reason: Retrieved the requested DeepWiki architecture overview and the pinned source README after direct page access failed. Subpages returned source files rather than deeper wiki chapters.
Per-URL crawl status clearly identified an unavailable old announcement, preventing use of an unverified funding record.
Returned full funding articles for Furo, OuterSignal, Sovera with amounts, investors, and product detail needed for ICP evaluation.

cost.note: One basic page costs one credit with parsers: []; a PDF is returned as base64. Firecrawl bills a returned target 403/404 document, but no-document failures are free.

input.note: Pass parsers: [] to keep PDF URLs at the flat one-credit rate; PDF content is then returned as base64. JSON, question, highlights, threat scans and other charged options are excluded. A target 403/404 document is billable; an upstream request with no document is free.

siblings.call_template: treg call keenable.web.fetch --query url=https://docs.keenable.ai/ --query max_chars=500 --query live=false

cost.note: The configured purchased package costs $4 per 1,000 requests. Keenable documents one credit per authenticated search or fetch, including both search modes and indexed/live fetch; no evidence says rejected requests are free, so platform calls are metered per request. BYOK calls are unmetered by treg.

max_chars.note: Longer content is truncated and a notice is appended after the cut.

live.note: Fetch directly from the source instead of using the indexed copy; also supports URLs absent from the index.

prompt.note: Return only the extraction requested here instead of the full page.

input.note: The live response returned published_at as a Unix timestamp even though the OpenAPI schema says string; treg relays the provider value unchanged.

siblings.name: Fetch a web page
siblings.summary: Retrieve clean Markdown from a public HTML or PDF URL.

cost.note: Markdown Fetch is billed per successful request by mode and JavaScript rendering.

input.note: Structured output has a separate catalog tool because providing schema adds $0.001 to any mode and renderJs combination. A team's own raw tool can request raw page bytes.

siblings.name: Fetch rendered web content
siblings.summary: Fetch a public HTTP(S) page and return LLM-ready content

cost.note: One successful API response consumes one prepaid call; failures are free.

assert_status_code.note: Expected origin HTTP status, 100-599. A different status is rejected; otherwise a rendered error page is a successful capture.

base.note: Resolve relative links against the requested URL (initial, default) or the final URL after redirects (final).

detach_invisibles.note: Drop display:none elements from the page.

engine.note: auto (default; lightweight HTTP first, a browser when needed), browser, or curl (no JavaScript).

keep_img_data_url.note: Keep inline data: images in Markdown.

locale.note: Browser locale as a language tag, 2-64 characters. Defaults to the browser's own.

markdown_chunking.note: true, h1-h5, structured or s1-s5: split the Markdown and return chunks.

max_tokens.note: Integer 500-10,000,000. Trim content to this many tokens.

no_gfm.note: true, false or table: disable GitHub-flavored Markdown, or only its tables.

page_timeout.note: Seconds from 1 through 180 for page loading and browser operations. Cannot extend the total request budget set by timeout.

preset.note: Option preset. Fills only the options the request leaves unset.

referer.note: HTTP(S) URL sent as the Referer.

remove_overlay.note: Remove modal and cookie-banner overlays from the page.

remove_selector.note: CSS selector removed before extraction, 1-2,048 characters; POST also accepts a list of 1-16 selectors.

respond_timing.note: Page readiness condition to reach before responding.

respond_with.note: Output format: content (default; main content as Markdown, or the whole page when extraction keeps too little), markdown (whole page as Markdown), html, text, frontmatter (content plus front matter), or a '+' combination such as markdown+frontmatter. For screenshots use /api/web/screenshot.

retain_images.note: Images to keep: all (default), alt (alt text only) or none.

retain_links.note: Links to keep: all (default), text (link text only), none, or gpt-oss (citation format with a links summary).

retain_media.note: How video, audio and embedded video appear: none, text, link (default), image or html.

robots_txt.note: User agent, 1-256 characters, to check against the site's robots.txt; disallowed URLs are rejected.

target_selector.note: CSS selector to extract, 1-2,048 characters; POST also accepts a list of 1-16 selectors. Implies waiting for the selector. Match-all selectors are rejected.

token_budget.note: Integer 1-10,000,000. Reject the page when its token count exceeds the budget.

url.note: Public HTTP(S) URL to capture, 1-8,192 characters. Include http:// or https://; bare domains are rejected. The host must be public, on port 80 or 443, without embedded credentials.

user_agent.note: User-Agent for the page request, 1-1,024 characters without control characters. Defaults to the browser's own.

wait_for_selector.note: CSS selector to wait for after navigation, 1-2,048 characters. POST also accepts a list of 1-16 selectors.

with_iframe.note: true, false or quoted: include iframe content before extraction.

with_images_summary.note: Add an images list to the response.

with_links_summary.note: true, false or all: add a links list to the response.

with_shadow_dom.note: Include open shadow DOM content before extraction.

timeout.note: Optional budget for the entire request in seconds, measured from gateway receipt until the response is ready to send. Includes admission, queueing and settlement. Must be greater than 0 and at most 90. On expiry, the call is not billed and returns 503 request_deadline_exceeded with retryable=true and a request ID. Omit to retain the standard server deadline.

siblings.name: web.extract — routed: best of 15 providers, own keys first
siblings.summary: Extract clean content from one web page — provider-native rows in `pages`

cost.note: NOT free: misses are billed too. the children's range $0–$0.01 per hit, 0% markup; you pay the child that served AND every child tried before it that bills a miss (5 of 15 do), up to X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost (default $1 a call). X-Treg-Route-Exclude them, or X-Treg-Route-Waterfall: 0, to pay for one provider only

input.note: Send everything you know about the subject — treg derives the rest (full_name ⇄ first+last), matches each provider on the variants it accepts ({url}) and sends each provider only the fields it wants. On a miss treg keeps trying providers, cheapest first, within X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost (default $1 per call; misses on per-success providers are free). Options ride as headers, never in the body: X-Treg-Route-Waterfall: 0 (stop at the first miss), X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost: <usd>, X-Treg-Route-Prefer / X-Treg-Route-Exclude: <provider>. The response is {output, raw, _treg: {served_by, tried}}; X-Treg-Served-By names the child.
